summary: Walkthrough of the Redwood Console tracing, error analysis and request logs for debugging production inference issues. Covered end-to-end flow from incoming request to kernel selection and KV cache hits, demonstrated tracing UI, examples of error analysis (bad prompts, model fallbacks), and how to export request logs for compliance. Agreed on next steps: run P99 latency benchmarks, share SOC2 docs, and schedule POC kickoff.
topics: Error analysis: root cause & sample failure cases
Debugging flows: reproduce -> trace -> snapshot -> rollback
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (CTO - AcmeCloud), Sofia Torres (ML Eng), Kevin Wu (DevOps), Anika Patel (Security), Liam (PM)

[00:00:10] Jordan: hi everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do a quick intro then jump into the redwood console - tracing, request logs, error analysis - walk through a couple of common debugging flows. Priya will demo and then we'll take questions.

[00:00:27] Marcus: Yep thanks Jordan. We, uh, mostly interested in debugging high 95/99 p lat issues and understanding what happens when we see model fallbacks. also compliance bits, SSO and KMS stuff.

[00:00:40] Priya: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Quick note, I might mis-pronounce some internal kernel names, transcription sometimes shows "KV cash" in the UI, but it's KV cache.

[00:00:52] Jordan: ha, yes the usual fireflies typos. Ok Priya, you can share your screen.

[00:01:10] Priya: Sharing now. Alright so this is the Redwood Console, top-level nav, I'm on the Observability -> Tracing tab. You can see a timeline of recent requests, each row is a request span, we surface latency, tokens, model variant, and route policy.

[00:01:40] [Priya] So here we have an example spike at 14:03 UTC, zooming in you can see subspans: frontend routing, batcher queue, kernel exec, kv-cache lookup, and response stream. The trace IDs link directly to the full request log and any artifacts (prompt snapshot, model logits sample).

[00:02:05] Sofia: quick q - are logits exported by default? we have concerns about PII in outputs.

[00:02:12] Priya: Good question - logits and raw token streams are disabled by default for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention. We support redaction and also allow you to only capture metadata (latency, tokens, model id) if you need strict limits.

[00:02:30] Anika: and KMS for logs? we need encryption-at-rest with our keys.

[00:02:35] Jordan: yes, for Private deployments we plug into customer KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys as an option, and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. I'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs after the call.

[00:02:50] [00:03:10] Priya: Back to the trace - notice the batcher queue subspan is long here, that's often a sign of small-batch inefficiency during bursts. Console will surface batching efficiency and suggest changing batch size / windowing or using AutoBatch policies.

[00:03:30] Kevin: is the batcher per-tenant or per-gpu-pool? curious about isolation.

[00:03:35] Priya: It's per-serving-pool. For Dedicated you can dedicate pools per-customer, and you can pin models so batching won't mix tenants in the same pool. There's also routing policies to route high-priority traffic to reserved pools.

[00:03:55] [00:04:20] Priya: Now we'll look at a failed request. The trace shows a model fallback - primary model hit a memory limit and the runtime fell back to a quantized variant. You can see the exact kernel error in the error subspan: "OOM during KV cache allocation" - that gets surfaced along with the prompt snapshot.

[00:04:45] Marcus: so fallback is automatic? and can we disable it? sometimes fallback masks the root issue.

[00:04:52] Priya: Good point. Fallbacks are policy-driven. By default we fall back to a compatible variant to preserve availability. You can change that on a per-route basis: fail-fast (no fallback), warn-only (log), or auto-fallback. The Console lets you change and roll out that policy and also shows the impact of toggling it.

[00:05:10] [00:05:45] Priya: If you click into the request log, you get full timeline, token counts, per-kernel timings, and a diff view that highlights which step added most latency. There's also a flamegraph for compute-bound vs IO-bound time.

[00:06:00] Sofia: that flamegraph is super helpful. can we export these traces as JSON for our own analysis?

[00:06:07] Priya: yes, exportable as ndjson and you can push to S3 or our log-forwarder. For compliance we support retention policies, and request logs can be scrubbed before export.

[00:06:30] [00:06:50] Priya: Next demo - error analysis. Console groups similar errors into buckets, here we have prompt-induced hallucination flags, model-crash OOMs, and inference-time HTTP 5xx from upstream. You can triage by cluster, model, and route.

[00:07:05] Kevin: how do you detect hallucinations? we can't fully automate that.

[00:07:12] Priya: We don't claim perfect detection - it's heuristic based on regeneration behavior, hallucination classifiers you can plug in, and user feedback. Console surfaces candidate hallucinations - you review and label them for downstream alerts. That's part of the Redwood Optimize workflow for quality monitoring.

[00:07:35] [00:08:10] Priya: I'll show a debugging flow: reproduce -> trace -> snapshot -> rollback. You can replay a request in a safe sandbox using the exact model variant and kernel set; we snapshot the KV cache and prompt so reproduction is deterministic.

[00:08:28] Marcus: replay in prod? please clarify. we don't want replays hitting production models and affecting billing.

[00:08:34] Priya: Replays are sandboxed; they run in a restricted test runtime and do not consume customer quota. There's an option to run Replays in your Dedicated pool if you explicitly opt in.

[00:08:50] [00:09:05] Priya: Another useful bit - request-level metadata includes route, client-id, model-variant, kernel-version, quantization profile, and docker image tag. This helps root-cause when the rollout touched a bad kernel or a new quantization profile.

[00:09:24] Sofia: can we map traces back to our internal request id? yes?

[00:09:30] Priya: Absolutely. We accept customer metadata headers (x-acme-request-id) and surface that in the trace. You can search by that id.

[00:09:45] [00:10:10] Priya: Now quick look at Request Logs table - filterable by status code, model, latency, tokens, and custom tags. You can set up alerts: e.g., P99 > 800ms for route X, or error-rate > 1% over 5m.

[00:10:30] Anika: does alerting integrate with PagerDuty / Slack?

[00:10:34] Jordan: yes webhook/PagerDuty/Slack, and we can also forward events to your SIEM.

[00:10:45] [00:11:05] Priya: We'll demonstrate a live search: filter to requests with kernel-exec > 300ms, then narrow by model-variant. Here, you can see a cluster of slow requests tied to a quantized variant deployed last week - looks like kernel version v1.2.4.

[00:11:25] Marcus: Did we recently toggle any auto-batching?

[00:11:30] Kevin: yes we changed windowing last week for cost reasons.

[00:11:33] Priya: Ok that matches - the Optimize tab had recommended a smaller window for throughput, but that raised P99. We can show a diff of quality vs latency for that change.

[00:11:50] [00:12:20] Priya: Error drilldown shows stack traces and the exact libc error for OOMs (best-effort capture, sometimes truncated). For transient network 5xx we show upstream host and retry policy. You can annotate and assign to an oncall, and it creates a ticket with the trace link.

[00:12:38] Liam: can those tickets be auto-created in Jira?

[00:12:42] Priya: Yep Jira and ServiceNow integrations supported.

[00:12:50] [00:13:10] Priya: I'll show how to use the snapshot and rollback: when you find a bad rollout you can roll back to previous model tag or kernel set right from the trace; the Console also shows the delta of served traffic during the rollout so you can see exposure.

[00:13:30] Marcus: that delta view - can we set canary percentages automatically? we want gradual ramp with automatic revert on error.

[00:13:36] Priya: Yes Canary rollouts supported with health checks: if error-rate breaches threshold, the system can automatically revert. Policies are configurable per-route.

[00:13:50] [00:14:10] Priya: Quick note on privacy - we redact prompts on export if configured, and we can obfuscate tokens. For regulatory workloads we recommend Private deployment with customer KMS and VPC peering.

[00:14:30] Anika: for Private, how does auditing work? we need tamper-evident logs.

[00:14:36] Jordan: audit logs are shipped with append-only storage options and HMAC signing. We'll include a section in the SOC2 docs for that.

[00:14:55] [00:15:30] Priya: Now a short demo of tracing correlation - linking model metric anomalies to trace clusters. Here we show a spike in tokenization time that correlated with a recent tokenizer change. The Console surfaces correlated events (deployments, config changes) next to trace timeline.

[00:16:00] Sofia: interesting. can we tag traces with dataset or prompt template?

[00:16:06] Priya: Yes, you can add custom tags at call-time. We commonly ingest prompt_template names, customer_biz_unit, and A/B test ids. That makes grouping and regression detection easier.

[00:16:25] [00:16:45] Priya: A note about request logs retention: default 30 days for hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private. Export to your S3 or GCS for long-term storage; we support lifecycle rules.

[00:16:58] Kevin: what's export throughput? our footprint is big.

[00:17:02] Priya: We stream logs in parallel and can provision an export pipeline for high-volume customers. We'll size a plan based on your traffic profile - Kevin, please send that sample traffic profile, that'll help.

[00:17:20] [00:17:50] Priya: Finally, quick callouts on Optimize: it will recommend batching/quantization changes per-route and estimate cost delta and P99 impact. You can preview recommendations in a dry-run.

[00:18:10] Marcus: have you seen quantization regressions? we care about quality.

[00:18:16] Priya: Sometimes - that's why we tie Optimize to eval suites. We recommend small step quantization and quality gating using your prompts. You can set auto-rollout only if eval pass rate > X.

[00:18:35] [00:19:00] Jordan: ok we're at about 19 minutes in - maybe take some live questions and then we'll recap next steps.

[00:19:10] Sofia: (laughs) sorry my connection dropped, i meant Sofia - quick Q: on the replay sandbox, can we inject faults? like simulating GPU throttling?

[00:19:22] Priya: You can simulate throttling and network latency in the sandbox, yes. It's useful for SRE root-cause tests.

[00:19:35] Anika: On the SOC2 docs - i need to confirm data residency controls, we operate in EU exclusively.

[00:19:41] Jordan: For EU customers we can lock data to EU regions in Hosted; Dedicated and Private are options too. We'll add region-specific retention info to the packet I send.

[00:19:55] [00:20:15] Jordan: Quick poll - would you prefer Redwood Dedicated POC or start Hosted with strict data controls?

[00:20:21] Marcus: Dedicated POC sounds right given compliance and expected volume.

[00:20:25] Kevin: agree, Dedicated gives us isolation and predictable throughput.

[00:20:30] Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with a POC proposal and pricing.

[00:20:40] [00:21:05] Priya: Any other questions?

[00:21:12] Liam: one last: can the Console show per-token cost breakdown? our finance team asks that often.

[00:21:18] Priya: yes cost per-token and route-level cost are available; there's also token-level breakdown to attribute cost to prompts vs generation.

[00:21:30] [00:22:00] Jordan: Alright let's do a short recap. Priya will run the P99 benchmark using Acme sample prompts and try to reproduce the OOM/fallbacks. Priya will share the benchmark results by 2026-02-17. Jordan will send SOC2, KMS, and pricing docs by Friday 2026-02-12. Kevin to provide traffic profile and allowlist so we can size Dedicated pool. We'll schedule a POC kickoff for week of 2026-02-23.

[00:22:28] Marcus: sounds good. Also can you include a quick note about canary auto-revert thresholds?

[00:22:34] Jordan: yes will include that.

[00:22:40] [00:22:55] Priya: thanks everyone for the time. If you hit any issues after we send access, DM Jordan and we'll hop on a debug session.

[00:23:05] Marcus: Thanks. That was helpful.

[00:23:10] [end of transcript - remaining time used for follow-up 1:1 chats and a short break]
